chosen: The Render method utilizes the null-coalescing operator (??) to provide a default value if the input is null. When supplied is null, ?? evaluates the right side, returning "(unset)". When supplied is an empty string "", it is not null, so ?? skips the right side and returns the empty string unchanged. When supplied is "ready", it is also not null, so the method returns "ready" directly. The ?? operator specifically checks for a reference type being null (System.NullReferenceException condition), not whether the string content is empty.
rejected: The Render method uses ?? to check if the string length is zero. If supplied is null or an empty string "", the operator triggers and returns "(unset)". However, if supplied contains the text "ready", the operator sees a non-empty value and returns it as is. This logic incorrectly treats empty strings as equivalent to null for the purpose of this specific rendering function.
